description: Electrex Flash 96 and Flash D multifunction energy analyzers: voltages, currents, powers, power factors, THD, demand, energy counters and setup registers
source: Flash D Electric Energy Analyzer User Manual (and Flash N Electric Energy Analyzer User Manual (file name Flash 96))

sources.title: Flash D Electric Energy Analyzer User Manual
sources.version: Version 8, November 2005 (84 pages), section 9 Modbus Protocol
sources.note: Register mapping 9.4 (holding 0 to 139, input 200 to 376, coils 64 to 70)

sources.title: Flash N Electric Energy Analyzer User Manual (file name Flash 96)
sources.note: Same register mapping as the Flash D manual (the text of the holding and input register tables is identical)

notes: Electrex Flash 96 and Flash D multifunction meters (the manuals are titled Flash N and Flash D).

Modbus RTU or ASCII (selected in the communication menu), slave address and transmission delay (default 100 ms) set on the meter; the speed is 2400 to 38400 bps, with data bits, parity and stop bits selectable. The manual gives no factory defaults for these, so no serial settings are fixed in this map. Needs the optional RS485 or RS232 module.

Addresses are the register numbers printed in the manual; they are written here as printed, address base 0. Holding registers 0 to 139 are the setup area, input registers 200 and up are the measurements (the manual's 'FLASH D original registers'), and coils 64 to 70 are the commands. A float or 32-bit value takes two registers and a 64-bit value four; the manual numbers each word.
Big-endian byte and word order is the default (Motorola-like); holding register 70 and the coils 64 and 65 swap it.

Several measurement registers change meaning with the wiring (3P4W, 3P3W and so on): the description of each register lists the wirings; the two readings of one register are given in its name and description.

Energy counters are unsigned 32-bit (two registers) or 64-bit (four registers, high resolution) integers in the manual's unit written 'kWh/10', 'Wh/10', etc.; the scale 0.1 reads this as one count = 0.1 of the unit. The manual does not state the signedness of the integers; unsigned is assumed.

The backward-compatibility input area (addresses 0 to 199, the Kilo layout), the old coils 0 to 18, and the parameter selection tables for the analog outputs and alarms (9.4.2) are not mapped; the analog out and alarm registers are listed, with the index tables left to the manual. Bitmapped registers are listed as 16-bit words with the bit meaning in the description.
Written from the manufacturer's manual; not tested on a device.

registers.description: Bitmap: swap bytes (0 standard, 1 swapped), swap words, swap doublewords, swap words in float values; standard is Motorola-like (big endian), swapped is Intel-like. Write the same bit combination in both the low and the high part of the register; the byte swap setting is then meaningless for this register.

registers.name: Reset (warm boot)
registers.description: Reinitialize the device, the counters are not reset. Triggered on the leading edge; reads always 1.

registers.name: Clear energy counters
registers.description: Reset all the energy counters. Triggered on the leading edge; reads always 1.

registers.name: Power integration synchronization
registers.description: Synchronize the integration time. Triggered on the leading edge; reads always 1.

registers.name: Clear average powers
registers.description: Reset all the power values in moving average. Triggered on the leading edge; reads always 1.

registers.name: Clear maximum demand powers
registers.description: Reset all the power peak values. Triggered on the leading edge; reads always 1.
